mainTopic: The blood prohibition: which creatures are included (including the כוי), and light versus severe טומאה for people and animals
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא on the פסוק "כל דם לא תאכלו... לעוף ולבהמה". The ברייתא excludes the blood of שרצים, eggs, fish and grasshoppers, and it explains why the פסוק names both bird and animal. The גמרא reads the פסוקים as a כלל ופרט וכלל, which includes anything similar to bird and animal. It explains that this follows the school of רבי ישמעאל, even though the two generalizations are not alike. The extra phrase "אף כל" includes the blood of a כוי, which רב אדא בר אבין holds is a creature of its own kind. The גמרא then finds sources for the כוי's fat, נבלה, גיד הנשה, טומאה and שחיטה. Next it resolves a contradiction about whether people get light (food) טומאה: a living person's flesh can, but a dead body cannot. Finally, a משנה about which נבילות need מחשבה and הכשר leads to a debate between רב and רבי חייא about a piece of נבילה smaller than a כזית, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Excluding the blood of creeping creatures
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא excludes the blood of שרצים because they lack a severe form of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: I will exclude the blood of creeping creatures, since they do not have a severe form of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list of creatures whose blood is not included in the prohibition. Here it removes the blood of שרצים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bird and animal share certain features, and only creatures with those same features are included. One feature is a טומאה חמורה, a severe impurity. שרצים do have טומאה, but not the severe kind, so their blood is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: I will exclude (leave out of the rule)
Small creeping creatures (like mice and lizards)
A severe form of ritual impurity

phrases.english: I will exclude the blood of creeping creatures
since they do not have a severe impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list of exclusions begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood of שרצים is not included in the prohibition of blood, since they lack טומאה חמורה.

steps.title: Excluding the blood of eggs
steps.stepSummary: Blood found in eggs is excluded because eggs are not a kind of meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: I will exclude the blood of eggs, since they are not a type of meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא removes another item from the prohibition: blood found in eggs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A second feature that bird and animal share is that they are מין בשר, real flesh. An egg is not flesh. So the blood in it does not fall under this prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: Eggs
A type of meat/flesh

phrases.english: I will exclude the blood of eggs
since they are not a type of meat,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second exclusion based on a different shared feature.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood of eggs is excluded because eggs are not מין בשר.

steps.title: Excluding the blood of fish and grasshoppers
steps.stepSummary: Blood of fish and grasshoppers is excluded because these creatures are entirely permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The blood of fish and the blood of grasshoppers is excluded, since they are entirely permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list by removing the blood of fish and grasshoppers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A third shared feature of bird and animal is that not everything in them is permitted. Fish and grasshoppers are כולו היתר, completely permitted, so they do not match. That is why their blood is not forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Fish
Grasshoppers / locusts
Entirely permitted

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא builds a profile of bird and animal from three features: severe טומאה, real meat, and not entirely permitted. Any creature missing one of these features has its blood excluded.

phrases.english: the blood of fish, the blood of grasshoppers
since it is entirely permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of exclusions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood of fish and grasshoppers is not forbidden, since they are כולו היתר.

steps.title: Why the verse needs the word animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why both bird and animal are mentioned. If only bird were written, we might limit animals to those without כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does it say "of bird and of animal"? If we went only by the bird, we might say: just as a bird is something that has no כלאים, so too the animal must be one that has no כלאים!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a question about the wording of the פסוק. It shows a mistake we could make if the word "animal" were not there on its own, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that bird would set the pattern for animal. Birds have no כלאים issue in this context, so we might forbid the blood of only those animals that also have no כלאים. That would leave other animals' blood permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: If (we said) just as... (introduces a possible mistaken comparison)
Forbidden mixtures / crossbreeding of different species
Bird
Domestic animal

phrases.english: "Of bird and of animal"? Why both?

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה עוֹף שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ כִּלְאַיִם,
phrases.english: If we said: just as a bird has no כלאים,
so too an animal that has no כלאים!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָעוֹף וְלַבְּהֵמָה אִי מָה עוֹף שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ כִּלְאַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the exclusions to why the פסוק lists both categories.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the word "בהמה" in the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without a separate word for animal, the bird's feature (no כלאים) could limit which animals are included.

steps.title: The word animal stands on its own
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק writes "ולבהמה" separately, so animals are not limited by the bird's features.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the verse says: "and of animal."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the worry from the last step. The separate word for animal shows that all animals are included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because בהמה is named on its own, it is not judged by the bird's pattern. So animal blood is forbidden whether or not that animal has any connection to כלאים.

keyTerms.meaning: "The verse teaches," which introduces the wording that solves the problem

phrases.english: The verse says: "and of animal."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: an independent word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Animals would be limited to those without כלאים, like birds.
steps.terutzMaskana: All animals' blood is forbidden, because בהמה is mentioned on its own.

steps.title: Why the verse needs the word bird
steps.stepSummary: If only animal were written, we might limit birds to those not subject to אם על הבנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we went only by the animal, we might say: just as an animal is not part of the law of the mother with her young, so too the bird must be one that is not part of the law of the mother with her young!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the ברייתא raises the opposite worry: that animal would set the pattern for bird. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law of אם על הבנים applies only to birds, never to animals. If animal set the pattern, we might forbid the blood of only those birds that this law does not cover. That would wrongly permit the blood of the other birds.

keyTerms.meaning: The mother bird with her young: the law of sending away the mother bird (שִׁלּוּחַ הַקֵּן)

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה בְּהֵמָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ בְּאֵם עַל הַבָּנִים,
phrases.english: If we said: just as an animal is not part of the law of the mother with her young,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עוֹף שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּאֵם עַל הַבָּנִים!
phrases.english: so too a bird that is not part of the law of the mother with her young!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה בְּהֵמָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ בְּאֵם עַל הַבָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 4 in the other direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the word "עוף" alongside בהמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without a separate word for bird, the animal's feature (not part of אם על הבנים) could limit which birds are included.

steps.title: Bird and animal each stand on their own
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק names both bird and animal, so neither is limited by the other's features.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the verse says: "of bird and of animal."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא solves the second worry the same way: both categories are written out, so all birds are included too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק names each group separately, neither group is narrowed by the other. So all birds' blood is forbidden, and so is all animals' blood.

keyTerms.meaning: "Of bird and of animal," the two categories named in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק names both עוף and בהמה so that neither one limits the other. All birds and all animals are included.

phrases.english: The verse says: "of bird and of animal."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem raised in step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Birds would be limited to those not subject to אם על הבנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: All birds' blood is forbidden as well.

steps.title: Challenge: read the verse as a general term followed by a detail
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests reading "כל דם" as a כלל and "bird and animal" as a פרט. That would limit the prohibition to bird and animal only.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: "any blood" is a general statement, and "bird and animal" is a detail. With a general statement followed by a detail, the general includes only what is in the detail. So bird and animal, yes; anything else, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's whole reading. It uses a standard rule of how to read פסוקים, and by that rule only bird and animal would be forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the rule of כלל ופרט, the general word "כל דם" is narrowed to just the listed details. That would mean no other creature's blood is forbidden at all, even if it shares the features of bird and animal. This threatens the ברייתא's method of including other creatures that share those features.

keyTerms.meaning: "But say instead," which proposes another reading as a challenge
A general statement followed by a specific detail
The general includes only what is in the detail
Anything else

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the conclusion. The גמרא is only raising a challenge here. The next step answers it with a second generalization in the next פסוק.

phrases.english: But say: "any blood" is a general statement,
"bird and animal" is a detail,
a general statement followed by a detail,
the general includes only what is in the detail,
so bird and animal, yes,
anything else, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from explaining the ברייתא to challenging its method of reading the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's method of including any creature that shares the features of bird and animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the rule of כלל ופרט, "כל דם" is limited to the listed details, so only bird and animal blood would be forbidden.

steps.title: A second generalization makes it a three-part pattern
steps.stepSummary: The next פסוק, 'whoever eats any blood,' is a second generalization. That turns the pattern into כלל ופרט וכלל, which includes anything similar to the detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק goes on to say 'A soul that eats any blood.' This is a second generalization. So we have a generalization, a detail, and another generalization. In that case we include only things that are similar to the detail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from step 8. There is a second generalization after the detail, so the prohibition is not limited to bird and animal alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, 'כל דם' followed by 'bird and animal' looked like a plain כלל ופרט, which would cover only bird and animal. Now a second כלל appears afterward. Under the rule of כלל ופרט וכלל, we widen the law to anything that resembles the detail.

keyTerms.meaning: It went back and generalized again (a second general statement)
A generalization, then a detail, then another generalization. A rule for reading פסוקים.
Similar to the detail. Only things that resemble the named examples are included.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the boundary of the blood prohibition. It covers more than birds and animals, but only things that share their features.

phrases.english: "A soul that eats any blood"
it went back and generalized again.
A generalization, a detail, and a generalization:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט.
phrases.english: you may include only things similar to the detail.

steps.triggerLanguage: נפש אשר תאכל כל דם חזר וכלל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by pointing to a second generalization.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to more text in the פסוקים that changes how the rule applies
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only כלל ופרט, the prohibition would cover only bird and animal blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is כלל ופרט וכלל, so anything similar to bird and animal is included.

steps.title: The two generalizations do not match
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the first generalization is a לאו and the second is כרת, so they are not the same kind of generalization.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the last generalization is not like the first one. The first generalization is a plain prohibition (a לאו). The last generalization carries the punishment of כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges using כלל ופרט וכלל here. The two 'generalizations' are different from each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For this rule to work, the two generalizations normally need to match. Here the first ("you shall eat no blood") is a לאו, while the second ("that soul shall be cut off") is a כרת. So maybe they should not be read together as one כלל ופרט וכלל.

keyTerms.meaning: The first generalization
The last generalization
A plain negative commandment
Being 'cut off', a severe heavenly punishment

phrases.english: But the last generalization is not similar
to the first generalization!
The first generalization is a plain prohibition,
and the last generalization is כרת!

steps.triggerLanguage: והא לא דמי כללא בתרא לכללא קמא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the method used in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using כלל ופרט וכלל for the blood פסוקים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two generalizations differ (לאו and כרת), so they may not form a valid כלל ופרט וכלל.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל uses the rule anyway
steps.stepSummary: This תנא is from the school of רבי ישמעאל, which uses כלל ופרט even when the two generalizations are not alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: This תנא is from the school of רבי ישמעאל. They learn from generalizations and details even in a case like this, where the last generalization is not like the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. It explains that this ברייתא follows a school that does not require the two generalizations to match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection assumed that matching generalizations are required. The answer is that the school of רבי ישמעאל does not require this. So the derivation in step 9 stands for this תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study house) of רבי ישמעאל
The method of reading פסוקים by generalizations and details
The method of reading פסוקים by inclusions and exclusions
We expound / derive from the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: Under the school of רבי ישמעאל, כלל ופרט וכלל works even when the two generalizations are of different types (here, לאו and כרת).

phrases.english: This תנא is from the school of רבי ישמעאל:
we expound [inclusions and exclusions and] generalizations and details
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording. Some versions do not have them.

phrases.english: even in a case like this,
even though it is not similar,
the last generalization to the first generalization.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies which תנא's method the ברייתא follows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two generalizations must match for כלל ופרט וכלל to apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: The school of רבי ישמעאל applies the rule even when the generalizations differ.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא's features of the detail
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's list of what bird and animal have in common, to look at it more closely next.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: with a generalization, a detail, and a generalization, you include only things similar to the detail. The detail clearly speaks of something that can have light impurity and severe impurity, can be forbidden or permitted, and is a kind of meat. So too, we include anything that can have light and severe impurity, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes the ברייתא's list of features word for word so it can examine that list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three features define the 'detail' (bird and animal): they can carry both light and severe impurity, they can be forbidden or permitted, and they are a type of meat. Anything sharing these features is included in the blood prohibition. The questions about this list come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Explicit, clearly stated
A light form of ritual impurity
A severe form of ritual impurity
Can be forbidden or permitted
A type of meat

phrases.english: The Master said:
A generalization, a detail, and a generalization:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְעֵין הַפְּרָט,
phrases.english: you may include only things similar to the detail.
Just as the detail is explicit,
an item that can have a light impurity
and a severe impurity,
and that can be forbidden or permitted,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and that is a type of meat,
so too, every item that has
light impurity and severe impurity, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר מר כלל ופרט וכלל אי אתה דן אלא כעין הפרט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא to analyze the features it lists.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything that can have light and severe impurity, can be forbidden or permitted, and is a type of meat is included in the blood prohibition.

steps.title: What does 'so too anything' come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא's phrase 'אף כל' adds beyond bird and animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The phrase 'so too anything' that the ברייתא teaches: what does it come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what extra case the words 'אף כל' in the ברייתא are meant to add. This question sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already listed bird and animal and left out humans, creeping creatures, fish and grasshoppers. So the words 'anything similar' must be adding some new creature, and the גמרא wants to know which one.

keyTerms.meaning: To include; to bring in an extra case
So too anything (similar to the detail)

phrases.english: 'So too anything,' which it teaches
phrases.notes: This is the phrase from the ברייתא we looked at in step 12, about anything that shares the features of bird and animal.

phrases.english: what does it come to include?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the ברייתא's list quoted in step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which extra creature the phrase 'אף כל' includes

steps.title: It includes the blood of a כוי
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אבין says the phrase includes the blood of a כוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אבין said: It comes to include the blood of a כוי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אבין answers that 'אף כל' adds the blood of a כוי, so eating it is forbidden too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כוי is a creature that does not fit neatly as a domestic animal or a wild animal. Because it is not clearly an 'animal' in the usual sense, a special phrase is needed to include its blood.

keyTerms.meaning: A creature that is not clearly a domestic animal or a wild animal
Its blood

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Avin said:
To include the blood of a koy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אָבִין לְאֵתוֹיֵי דָּמוֹ שֶׁל כּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase includes the blood of a כוי

steps.title: If the כוי is only a doubt, why would we need a פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב אדא בר אבין holds about the כוי, and challenges the idea that it is just a doubtful case.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does he hold? If he holds that a כוי is a doubtful case, do we need a פסוק to forbid a doubt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב אדא בר אבין's view of the כוי. If the כוי were only a doubtful case, there would be no need for a פסוק to include it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we just don't know whether the כוי is an animal or a wild animal, we would forbid its blood anyway because of the doubt. A פסוק is not needed for that. So the idea that the כוי is a doubt does not fit with saying a phrase comes to include it.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds; his view is
A doubt; a case we are unsure about
Is a פסוק needed?

phrases.english: What does he hold?
If he holds that a koy is a doubtful case,
is a verse needed to forbid a doubt?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָסָבַר? אִי קָסָבַר כּוֹי סְפֵיקָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning behind step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אבין's claim that a פסוק phrase is needed to include the כוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A doubtful case is forbidden without a פסוק, so if the כוי is a doubt, the phrase would be pointless

steps.title: The כוי is a creature of its own kind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב אדא בר אבין holds the כוי is a separate kind of creature.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he holds that a כוי is a creature of its own kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב אדא בר אבין sees the כוי as a בריה בפני עצמה, its own category, not a doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כוי is truly neither a domestic animal nor a wild animal, the words 'bird and animal' would not cover it. That is exactly why the extra phrase 'אף כל' is needed to include its blood.

keyTerms.meaning: A creature of its own kind, in a separate category

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אדא בר אבין, the כוי is a separate kind of creature, so its blood is forbidden only because of the extra phrase 'אף כל'.

phrases.english: Rather, he holds
that a koy is a creature of its own kind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא קָסָבַר כּוֹי בְּרִיָּה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the כוי is its own category, not a doubt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כוי is a doubtful case, so no פסוק would be needed
steps.terutzMaskana: The כוי is a separate creature, so a פסוק is needed to include its blood

steps.title: Where do we learn that the כוי's fat is forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: Having found the source for the כוי's blood, the גמרא asks about its fat and answers from the word 'כל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found its blood. From where do we know its fat? From 'any fat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source that the כוי's חלב is forbidden, and answers with the פסוק 'any fat'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the כוי is its own kind, every prohibition needs its own source. The word 'כל', meaning 'any', in the פסוק about fat is read as including the fat of a כוי.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (a source)
From where do we know it?
Forbidden fat

phrases.english: We have found its blood;
its fat, from where do we know?
From 'any fat.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:23. The extra word 'any' is what brings in the כוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 16: since the כוי is its own kind, it needs a source for each prohibition
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a כוי's fat is forbidden

steps.title: Where do we learn that the כוי's carcass is forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source for the כוי's נבלה and answers from 'any carcass'.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know its carcass? From 'any carcass.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know that a כוי that died without proper שחיטה is forbidden as נבלה. It answers with the פסוק 'any carcass'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like the fat. The word 'כל' in the פסוק about נבלה is read as including the כוי.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: Its carcass, from where do we know?
From 'any carcass.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 17, now for נבלה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a כוי's carcass is forbidden

steps.title: The כוי's גיד הנשה is forbidden because it has a כף הירך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the כוי's גיד הנשה is forbidden, and answers that the law depends on the כף הירך, which the כוי has.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know the גיד הנשה? The תורה made it depend on the כף הירך, and this creature has a כף הירך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the כוי's גיד הנשה. It answers without a new extra word: the law follows the כף הירך, and the כוי has one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the answer is different from fat and נבלה. The פסוק ties the גיד הנשה to the thigh socket, not to the type of creature. So any creature with that body part, including the כוי, is included.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve, forbidden to eat
The spoon-shaped part of the thigh, the hip socket
The תורה made it depend on

steps.whatToRemember: The כוי's blood, fat and נבלה each need the extra word 'כל', but its גיד הנשה is forbidden simply because it has a כף הירך.

phrases.english: The sciatic nerve, from where do we know?
The Merciful One made it depend on the spoon of the thigh,
phrases.notes: בראשית 32:33, 'the גיד הנשה which is on the כף הירך.'

phrases.english: and this one has a spoon of the thigh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of the כוי's prohibitions, but uses a different kind of source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a כוי's גיד הנשה is forbidden
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The law depends on having a כף הירך, and the כוי has one

steps.title: Source for the כוי's impurity and slaughter: logic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the כוי's carcass is טמא and that שחיטה works for it. It answers with סברא: since the תורה treats the כוי like a בהמה in everything else, the same is true here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its impurity and slaughter, from where do we know them? From logic. Since the תורה included the כוי like a domestic animal in all the other matters, its impurity and its slaughter are also like a domestic animal's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks its last source question about the כוי, this time about its טומאה and its שחיטה. It answers that no פסוק is needed, because simple logic shows it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier steps each law (blood, fat, נבלה, גיד הנשה) had a פסוק or a reason. Here the גמרא argues from a pattern. The תורה already treated the כוי like a בהמה in all those areas, so it is logical to treat its טומאה and שחיטה the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Logical reasoning (not a פסוק)
Its ritual impurity (here, of its carcass)
Kosher ritual slaughter
The Torah included it

steps.whatToRemember: The כוי is treated like a בהמה for blood, fat, נבלה, גיד הנשה, טומאה and שחיטה.

phrases.english: Its impurity and slaughter, from where do we know them?
From logic: since in all the other matters
the Merciful One included it like a domestic animal,
its impurity and its slaughter are also like a domestic animal's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Last in the series of source questions about the כוי (steps 17-19).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the כוי has טומאה like a בהמה and that שחיטה permits it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סברא: since the תורה treats it like a בהמה in every other area, it is the same for טומאה and שחיטה.

steps.title: Human blood excluded because people lack light impurity, contradicted by a משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-quotes the ברייתא: human blood is excluded because people have severe טומאה but not light טומאה. It then cites a משנה saying that flesh cut from a person needs מחשבה and הכשר, which means it can become טמא as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: I will exclude the blood of two-legged beings, since they have severe impurity but not light impurity. But contrast this with a משנה: one who cuts flesh from a person needs intent and being made susceptible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the ברייתא and sets up a contradiction with a משנה. After a side discussion (steps 22-25), step 27 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says people have only 'severe' טומאה, meaning the טומאה of a dead body, and not the 'light' טומאה of food. The משנה about cutting flesh from a person sets conditions (מחשבה and הכשר) for it to become טמא as food. That suggests human flesh can carry food-טומאה, which would be the 'light' טומאה the ברייתא denied.

keyTerms.meaning: Two-legged beings, meaning humans
Severe impurity, the impurity of a corpse
Light impurity, the impurity of food
Intent to use something as food
Making food able to become טמא through contact with water or certain liquids

steps.confusionAlert: 'Light' and 'severe' here are not about how strict a law is. They are two different types of טומאה: food-טומאה versus corpse-טומאה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: אוֹצִיא דַּם מְהַלְּכֵי שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: The Master said: I will exclude the blood of two-legged beings,
since they have severe impurity
but do not have light impurity.
But contrast this with a משנה: one who cuts flesh from a person
needs intent and being made susceptible.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: אוֹצִיא דַּם מְהַלְּכֵי שְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the כוי and back to an earlier line of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that humans have no light (food) טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה sets conditions for human flesh to become טמא as food, so food-טומאה does apply to human flesh.

steps.title: Why the משנה needs intent at all
steps.stepSummary: Before dealing with the contradiction, the גמרא questions the משנה itself: why is separate מחשבה needed, when the act of cutting the flesh should already show intent?
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was difficult for us: why do I need intent? Let his cutting count as intent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask a question on the משנה it just quoted. Cutting flesh off a person seems to show already that he wants it as food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually מחשבה is needed to turn something into 'food' for טומאה purposes. But a person who actively cuts off flesh has clearly shown a plan for it. So why does the משנה add a separate requirement of מחשבה?

keyTerms.meaning: And it was difficult for us
Why do I need it?
The act of cutting

phrases.english: And it was difficult for us: why do I need intent?
Let his cutting count as intent!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Side question on the משנה quoted in step 21, asked before the contradiction is resolved.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cutting the flesh should itself be enough to show intent.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: he cut it for a dog
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that the משנה is about someone who cut the flesh to feed a dog. Intent to feed a dog does not count as intent for food, so a separate מחשבה is still needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש said: it is where he cut it for a dog, and intent for a dog is not intent.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the question from the last step by narrowing the case. The cutting was done for a dog.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cutting was for a dog, it does not show intent to use the flesh as human food. So the משנה still needs a real מחשבה, intent for it to be eaten as food, before it can carry food-טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: When he cut it to give to a dog
It does not count as intent

phrases.english: And ריש לקיש said: it is where he cut it for a dog,
and intent for a dog is not intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to cutting for a dog.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cutting itself should count as intent, so a separate מחשבה would be pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cutting was for a dog, which is not food-intent, so real מחשבה is still required.

steps.title: Challenge: food for a dog does count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש from a משנה: food meant for people stays טמא until even a dog would not eat it. This shows that being fit for a dog still counts as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is it not? But we learned: they stated a rule about impurity: anything set aside as human food is impure, until it becomes unfit even for a dog to eat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's claim that intent for a dog is not intent. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה says food keeps its טומאה as long as a dog could still eat it. That suggests dog-food still counts as 'food' for טומאה. If so, cutting flesh for a dog should count as intent, and ריש לקיש's answer seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule
Set aside as food for people
Until it becomes unfit even for a dog to eat

phrases.english: And is it not? But we learned,
they stated a rule about impurity:
anything set aside as human food is impure,
until it becomes unfit even for a dog to eat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's answer from step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that intent for a dog is not intent.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה shows that food stays food for טומאה as long as a dog can eat it, so dog-food seems to count as food.

steps.title: The dog standard only works for removing impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge against ריש לקיש. The משנה about 'until a dog won't eat it' is about removing טומאה from food that was once fit for people. Our case is about giving flesh the ability to become טמא, and for that the food must be fit for people.
steps.simpleTranslation: That משנה is about taking טומאה away. Since the food was fit for a person at the start, it does not lose its טומאה until even a dog won't eat it. Here we are talking about giving it the ability to become טמא. If it is fit for a person, it counts as fit for a dog. If it is not fit for a person, it does not count as fit for a dog.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by showing that the משנה about dog food deals with a different question from our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food that was already human food keeps its טומאה for a long time, until even a dog would refuse it. But to start being food that can become טמא, the item must be fit for people. Being fit for a dog alone is not enough. So intent to feed a dog cannot make the flesh count as food, and ריש לקיש stands.

keyTerms.meaning: to take טומאה away from something
to bring טומאה onto something (to make it able to become טמא)
fit for a person to eat
being eaten by a dog

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say dog food never matters. It matters for how long food stays טמא, but not for whether something counts as food in the first place.

phrases.english: That one is about removing impurity from it,
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the משנה from step 24, about food staying טמא until a dog won't eat it.

phrases.english: since at the start it was fit for a person,
to remove it from impurity
it must become unfit even for a dog to eat.
Here it is about bringing impurity onto it,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is our case of flesh cut from a person.

phrases.english: if it is fit for a person, it is fit for a dog,

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא חֲזֵי לְאָדָם – לָא חֲזֵי לְכֶלֶב.
phrases.english: if it is not fit for a person, it is not fit for a dog.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against ריש לקיש from step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases: removing טומאה versus starting to be able to become טמא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being fit for a dog always counts as food, so intent to feed a dog should be enough intent for food.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dog standard only keeps טומאה on food that was already human food. To start counting as food, it must be fit for people.

steps.title: Back to the contradiction: intent means light impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the main contradiction. Either way, the משנה requires מחשבה for human flesh. מחשבה only matters for טומאה קלה, the light טומאה of food. So human flesh can get טומאה קלה, which goes against the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either way, the משנה teaches that intent is needed, and intent is only needed for light טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The side question about the dog is finished. Now the גמרא repeats the original contradiction between the ברייתא and the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: However we explain the reason for the מחשבה, the משנה still requires it. מחשבה only makes sense if human flesh can become טמא as food, which is טומאה קלה. That goes against the ברייתא, which said people do not get טומאה קלה.

keyTerms.meaning: either way; whatever the explanation
light טומאה, like the טומאה of food

phrases.english: Either way, it teaches that intent is needed,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה from step 21 about flesh cut from a person.

phrases.english: and intent is for light impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side question about the dog (steps 22-25) and returns to the contradiction from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that people get only severe טומאה and not light טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires מחשבה. מחשבה is only needed for food טומאה, which is light טומאה. So people do get light טומאה.

steps.title: A living person versus a dead person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about flesh from a living person, which can get food טומאה. The ברייתא is talking about after death, when the body has severe טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies while the person is alive. But after death, he is טמא with severe טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying the משנה and the ברייתא are talking about two different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flesh cut from a living person can become טמא as food once there is מחשבה. After death the body is a מת, which has severe טומאה, so there is no place for light food טומאה. That is what the ברייתא means.

keyTerms.meaning: this rule applies only (in a certain case)
while alive
after death
severe טומאה, like the טומאה of a dead body

phrases.english: This applies while alive,
but after death,
he is impure with severe impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by time: alive versus after death
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא are about the same situation, so they disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a living person. The ברייתא is about a dead person, who has severe טומאה only.

steps.title: A dead animal also has only severe impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. If the ברייתא is about after death, then a dead animal should match. But a dead animal's flesh and its blood both carry severe טומאה. So why does the ברייתא say an animal gets light טומאה and a person does not?
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the matching case of an animal after death. If it is the flesh, it makes things טמא with severe טומאה. If it is the blood, it also makes things טמא with severe טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 27 by comparing a dead person to a dead animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא contrasts people with animals. But after death, an animal is a נבילה, and its flesh and blood both have severe טומאה, just like a dead person. So the contrast in the ברייתא no longer makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: the matching case
an animal
makes things טמא

phrases.english: The matching case with an animal after death:
if it is flesh, it makes things impure with severe impurity,
and if it is blood, it makes things impure with severe impurity,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is about after death
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After death, an animal's flesh and blood also have severe טומאה. So the ברייתא's contrast between people and animals falls apart.

steps.title: Proof that the blood of a dead animal is impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה as its source: about the blood of נבילות, בית שמאי say it is טהור and בית הלל say it is טמא. So according to בית הלל, the blood of a dead animal carries severe טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: the blood of נבילות, בית שמאי say it is טהור, and בית הלל say it is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for what it just claimed about an animal's blood after death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל say the blood of a נבילה is טמא like the נבילה itself, which means severe טומאה. This backs up the challenge in step 28. The next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: the blood of animals that died without שחיטה
they say it is טהור
they say it is טמא

phrases.english: As we learned: the blood of animal carcasses,
Beit Shammai say it is pure,
and Beit Hillel say it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim about blood in step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That the blood of a dead animal carries severe טומאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in עדיות: בית הלל say the blood of נבילות is טמא

steps.title: The ברייתא's rule is needed for a משנה about intent and הכשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's rule is needed for a משנה. That משנה teaches which kinds of נבילה need מחשבה and הכשר in order to get the טומאה of food.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is only needed for what we learned in a משנה: A carcass of a non-kosher animal anywhere, and a carcass of a kosher bird in villages, need intent to be eaten but do not need הכשר. A carcass of a kosher animal anywhere, and a carcass of a kosher bird or forbidden fat in the markets, need neither intent nor הכשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 28. It explains that the ברייתא's rule, that an animal gets light טומאה and a person does not, is needed for the case in this משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the ברייתא says an animal has 'light טומאה', it is not talking about the severe טומאה of a carcass or its blood. It means a dead animal's flesh can get the light טומאה of food, which the משנה discusses. Some נבילות need someone to plan to eat them (מחשבה) before they count as food, because people usually do not eat them. Others are normal food in their place and need no plan at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for; the גמרא shows what case a teaching is really about
An animal that died without proper שחיטה
Intent; a plan to eat something, which makes it count as food
Making food able to become טמא by getting it wet with certain liquids
Markets, places with many people where such food would be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מחשבה and הכשר. מחשבה makes something count as food. הכשר is getting food wet, which lets food that already counts as food become טמא.

phrases.english: It is only needed for that which we learned:
phrases.notes: "It" is the ברייתא's rule that an animal gets light טומאה but a person does not.

phrases.english: A carcass of a non-kosher animal in any place,
a carcass of a kosher bird in the villages –
phrases.notes: In villages there are few people, so nobody expects it to be eaten.

phrases.english: need intent, but do not need הכשר.
A carcass of a kosher animal in any place,
and a carcass of a kosher bird, and forbidden fat, in the markets –

phrases.aramaic: אֵין צְרִיכִין לֹא מַחְשָׁבָה וְלֹא הֶכְשֵׁר.
phrases.english: need neither intent nor הכשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 28, which step 29 backed up with the dispute about blood of נבילות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what case the ברייתא is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be about severe טומאה after death, so an animal's blood should make it match a person.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about an animal's flesh getting the light טומאה of food, as in the משנה about מחשבה and הכשר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה becomes the base text for the rest of the discussion between רב and רבי חייא.

steps.title: רב asks why a carcass needs intent at all
steps.stepSummary: רב asks רבי חייא why a נבילה would need מחשבה to get the light טומאה of food. It is already טמא with its own severe טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to רבי חייא: Why do I need intent for light טומאה? The carcass itself is already טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב challenges the משנה just quoted. He does not see why מחשבה would matter for a נבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מחשבה only lets something get טומאה קלה, the light טומאה of food. But a נבילה is already a source of severe טומאה on its own. So adding the light טומאה of food seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Light טומאה, such as the טומאה of food
It itself is a source of טומאה
Why do I need it? Asks what a rule adds

phrases.english: And רב said to רבי חייא:
Intent, why do I need it for light טומאה?
It itself is טומאה!
phrases.notes: He means a נבילה already carries the severe טומאה of a carcass.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the משנה brought in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that some נבילות need מחשבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A נבילה is already a source of severe טומאה, so making it able to get light food טומאה seems pointless.

steps.title: Less than an olive-size of carcass joined with other food
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers: the case is less than a כזית of נבילה, which is too small to carry carcass טומאה. It is joined with less than a כביצה of other food, and together they make a כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For example, where there is less than an olive-size of carcass, and he joined it to less than an egg-size of food, so that this and that together make an egg-size.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers רב's question. He gives a case where the light טומאה of food really does matter for a נבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נבילה only carries its severe טומאה if it is at least a כזית. Food only gets food טומאה if it is at least a כביצה. So a tiny piece of נבילה matters only as food, and it can join other food to reach a כביצה. For that it needs מחשבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Olive-size; the smallest amount of נבילה that carries its own טומאה
Egg-size; the smallest amount of food that gets food טומאה
Joining two small amounts together to reach a needed size

steps.whatToRemember: מחשבה matters for a נבילה only when it is less than a כזית and is joined with other food to make a כביצה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
For example, where there is less than an olive-size of carcass,
and he joined it to less than an egg-size of food,
so that this and that together make an egg-size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב's challenge from step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נבילה always carries severe טומאה, so food טומאה adds nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Less than a כזית of נבילה carries no carcass טומאה, so it matters only as food joined to other food.

steps.title: Then it should also need to be made wet
steps.stepSummary: רב challenges רבי חייא: if a small piece of נבילה is treated only as food, it should also need הכשר. The school of רבי ישמעאל taught that anything that will not end up with severe טומאה needs הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should also need הכשר. For the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: "On any sowing seed that is sown". Just as seeds are special in that they will never carry severe טומאה, and they need הכשר, so too anything that will never carry severe טומאה needs הכשר!
steps.whatsHappening: רב attacks רבי חייא's answer. If the small piece counts only as food, the משנה should also require הכשר, but the משנה said it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The school of רבי ישמעאל learns from the פסוק about seeds. Seeds can never carry severe טומאה, and they need הכשר. So anything that can never carry severe טומאה needs הכשר. A piece of נבילה smaller than a כזית carries no severe טומאה, so by this rule it should need הכשר too.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא's explanation that the משנה is about less than a כזית of נבילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Less than a כזית of נבילה never carries severe טומאה. By the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל, it should need הכשר, but the משנה says it does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a rule that the rest of the sugya will have to deal with: what can carry severe טומאה does not need הכשר, and what cannot carry it does.

steps.title: Ordinary food needs הכשר, but a small piece of נבילה does not
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers that the rule requiring הכשר applies only to ordinary food. A piece of נבילה smaller than a כזית would carry severe טומאה if it were completed to a כזית, so it does not need הכשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said to רב: That rule is said about ordinary foods, which have no piece of נבילה smaller than a כזית in them. But here, there is a piece of נבילה smaller than a כזית inside. If one added to it and made a full כזית, it would carry severe טומאה. So it does not need הכשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא defends his explanation against רב's challenge. He shows that the rule of the school of רבי ישמעאל does not apply to this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב argued that anything which will not end up with severe טומאה needs הכשר. רבי חייא answers that a small piece of נבילה is not in that group. If it were completed to a כזית it would be fully טמא as a carcass, so it is treated like something that can reach severe טומאה, and it does not need הכשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Contact with a liquid, which makes food able to become טמא

steps.whatToRemember: A piece of נבילה smaller than a כזית can join with other food to make a כביצה and get food טומאה. Even so, it does not need הכשר, because if it were completed to a full כזית it would carry severe טומאה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sizes. כזית (olive) is the amount needed for carcass טומאה. כביצה (egg) is the amount needed for food טומאה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps רבי חייא's explanation of the משנה standing. It also limits the rule of the school of רבי ישמעאל to ordinary foods.
